name: Deployment rollback recompute recovery
visibleRules: Recover the key committed in the already-authorized rollback intent; never derive it from the current controller, authority epoch or retry attempt.
All attempts for one rollback intent collectively create exactly one compensation effect.
Retry a lost completed-compensation response with the committed key and treat a deduplicated result as completion.
Report the rollback intent, controller, authority epoch, sent key and observed result truthfully.
Every supplied rollback intent is authorized and must reach the controller at least once.
No rollback-decision, cloud-provider, release-DAG or irreversible-effect policy is part of this family.
hiddenGradedRegion: The hidden suite samples only declared seed, controller-count, release-effect-width and crash-position dimensions. The target stratum contains two seeds per (nControllers, effects) cell for two, three and four controllers after compensation; one-controller and clean-compensation controls prove non-activation.

knobs.name: seed
knobs.purpose: selects deterministic release, region, compensation and rollback identity

knobs.name: nControllers
knobs.purpose: one controller cannot cross authority; two or more expose recovery under changed authority

knobs.name: effects
knobs.purpose: release-effect width, retained as a concentration and collision-control dimension

knobs.name: crashPosition
knobs.purpose: whether compensation is followed by uncertain recovery or a clean controller completion

authoritativeSources.name: authorized durable rollback intent
authoritativeSources.whatItSettles: the stable rollback identity, release, region, compensation and key committed before invocation
authoritativeSources.whyEngineCannotForge: The scenario generator creates the intent before subject execution. The subject may read it but cannot replace the value against which calls are graded.

authoritativeSources.name: deployment controller effect ledger
authoritativeSources.whatItSettles: how many compensation effects occurred for one rollback intent and under which keys
authoritativeSources.whyEngineCannotForge: The trial host owns the ledger and exposes only compensate(). The parent verifier receives a sealed copy after subject execution.

authoritativeSources.name: controller call ledger
authoritativeSources.whatItSettles: the exact compensation, key, controller and authority epoch on every call
authoritativeSources.whyEngineCannotForge: The facade records calls before returning completion and exposes no call-ledger handle through the subject interface.

referenceContract: Read the committed rollback key from the durable intent on every controller attempt.
Submit the unchanged release, region, compensation and logical rollback identity.
Treat first completion and deduplicated completion as successful recovery.
Report the actual key and authority epoch used.
Produce one compensation effect despite controller authority transfer.
fairnessConstraints: Every graded rule code appears in SPEC.md.
The committed rollback key and complete authorized compensation are visible in every recovery view.
No hidden cloud-provider, rollback-decision or reversibility convention is graded.
The four-cell probe distinguishes uncertainty, authority change and their interaction.
Hidden cases sample only declared dimensions.
cheatResistance: The controller call and effect ledgers are harness-owned and absent from the challenge package.
A no-op report fails the positive compensation floor.
A forged committed-key report is compared with the actual controller call.
The challenge leak profile excludes truth, verifier, selection and mutant artifacts.
The trial route preserves challenge, submission, transcript, verifier output and countability artifacts.
expectedFailureModes: Recomputing a rollback key from the current controller authority epoch.
Generating a fresh key from the recovery attempt after a lost result.
Reporting the committed key while sending a different key to the controller.
Refusing uncertain recovery and never applying the authorized compensation.
evidence: Built in Phase 13 from the pre-registered committed-authority recipe. The 72-point local grid and four-cell U x C probe show the recompute mutant fails only when compensation completion is uncertain and controller authority changes. The selected 24-scenario package retains 18 activated cases and 6 controls. This is local synthetic-controller transfer evidence, not frontier-agent or production-cloud evidence.
